claims.text: Room-temperature fracture toughness in single-phase FCC high-entropy alloys is governed by stacking-fault energy.
High stacking-fault energy favors deformation by dislocation slip.
Intermediate stacking-fault energy favors mechanical twinning.
Low stacking-fault energy favors martensitic transformation.
Alloys with intermediate stacking-fault energy retain the greatest toughness because twinning-induced plasticity enhances work hardening.
The baseline equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi alloy is single-phase FCC and recrystallized, with an average grain size of about 20 µm and stacking-fault energy of about 20 mJ/m².
Varying Mn from 10 at.% to 25 at.% shifts the stacking-fault energy from about 15 mJ/m² to about 35 mJ/m².
Stacking-fault energy controls the nucleation of deformation twins.
At a stacking-fault energy of approximately 25–30 mJ/m², deformation twins form and raise the work-hardening rate.
The increased work-hardening rate associated with twinning delays crack initiation.
At stacking-fault energies below 15 mJ/m², martensitic transformation embrittles the alloy.
At stacking-fault energies above 35 mJ/m², restricted slip reduces ductility.
The baseline equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi alloy has a room-temperature fracture toughness of approximately 120 MPa·m^0.5.
Fracture toughness will peak at a stacking-fault energy of approximately 25–30 mJ/m², corresponding to approximately 18 at.% Mn.
The peak fracture toughness will exceed the baseline by approximately 15–20%.
Alloys outside the 25–30 mJ/m² stacking-fault-energy window will have 10–30% lower toughness.
The hypothesis applies to single-phase FCC high-entropy alloys with grain sizes of 10–30 µm and stacking-fault energies of 15–40 mJ/m².
The hypothesis breaks down if second phases form or if grain size is below 5 µm or above 50 µm.
Mn contents above 25 at.% can be used to produce stacking-fault energies below 15 mJ/m².
Adding 5 at.% Al can be used to produce stacking-fault energies above 40 mJ/m².

contradictions.description: The intervention and prediction imply that increasing Mn from 10 to 25 at.% raises SFE from about 15 to 35 mJ/m², but the falsification design states that Mn above 25 at.% produces SFE below 15 mJ/m².

The hypothesis is bounded to SFE values of 15–40 mJ/m², while the proposed decisive falsification uses alloys below 15 or above 40 mJ/m². Results outside the stated validity range cannot decisively falsify the bounded hypothesis.
